# Axonius Cuts 22% of Israeli Devs in AI-Driven Restructuring


By OpenTools Team


·


November 10, 2026


Cybersecurity unicorn Axonius is cutting 66 jobs, including 22% of its Israeli developers, as it reshapes engineering around what its CEO calls a new AI‑driven way of working. It is a concrete signal of how AI is starting to replace developer headcount.


## 66 Jobs, 22% of Israeli Developers


Cybersecurity unicorn Axonius is preparing to cut 66 jobs, including 46 at its Israeli development center, as it reshapes its engineering organization around a new AI-driven approach to software development. The departures represent roughly 9% of its 722-person global workforce, but in Israel, where the company employs 207 people, about 22% have been summoned to pre-dismissal hearings,[CTech by Calcalist](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/9upwifo24) reported.


The cuts land even as the business grows: Axonius passed $200 million in annual recurring revenue in the first quarter of its fiscal 2027, up 35% year over year, and serves nearly 1,000 customers including more than 100 Fortune 1000 companies, per CTech.


## The CEO's Framing: AI-Driven, Not a Downturn


CEO Joe Diamond cast the reductions as a structural shift rather than a sign of weakness. "We've made changes to our engineering team, as we reshape how we build around a new AI-driven way of working," Diamond said in a statement reported by[CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/9upwifo24) . "Over the past several months, we've changed how our software gets built and we're adjusting our structure to match."


## Third Round of Cuts in Under a Year


This is Axonius's third workforce reduction in about a year. It laid off roughly 100 employees in November 2025,[BankInfoSecurity](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/deepwatch-axonius-carry-out-steep-layoffs-amid-surge-in-ai-a-30033) reported, then cut another 40 positions in February 2026, according to[CTech](https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/9upwifo24) . A company spokesperson framed the 2025 round as a "strategic business decision to sharpen our focus for future growth." Axonius raised a $200 million Series E extension co-led by Accel and Lightspeed in March 2024 at a $2.6 billion valuation.


## The Bigger Trend: Cybersecurity and AI Layoffs


Axonius is not alone. CrowdStrike cut 5% of its nearly 10,000-person workforce in 2025, saying "AI flattens our hiring curve," and data security vendor Varonis trimmed 5%, or roughly 120 employees,[BankInfoSecurity](https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/deepwatch-axonius-carry-out-steep-layoffs-amid-surge-in-ai-a-30033) reported. The pattern is consistent: late-stage security startups are trimming engineering headcount while reallocating toward AI and automation.


## The Developer-Anxiety Story


The Axonius cuts fit a broader shift across Israeli tech, where AI21 shut down its AI model development operation and laid off 60% of its staff, while Amdocs has also shed workers,[Ynet News](https://www.ynetnews.com/business/article/ryt113f9xfx) reported. The through-line is that AI tools are now reshaping how software itself gets built, and engineering teams are being resized to match.


## What It Means for Builders


Axonius is a useful signal because it is explicit about the cause. This is not a demand slump or a cost-cutting story tied to a downturn: the company is growing revenue 35% year over year and still cutting developers. The stated reason is that AI changed how the software gets written, so fewer people are needed to build it. For individual builders and freelancers, the takeaway is that the efficiency AI provides is now being applied to developer headcount itself, not just to the work.
